takeaways: No step of logging in may rely on a cognitive function test, such as remembering a password, transcribing a code or solving a puzzle, unless something helps.
Help can be another method that is not a test, such as a passkey or an email link, or support like pasting and password managers.
A password field passes if people can paste into it and password managers can fill it.
At AA, recognizing objects, or picking a photo the user provided, is allowed. 3.3.9 (AAA) removes that exception.
failures: Paste blocked in password or code fields
A distorted-text CAPTCHA with no alternative
One-time code fields that break when a code is pasted
check: Walk every login, sign-up and verify step and list what each asks people to remember, copy or solve.
Try a password manager and paste in every field of the flow.
For each test you find, name the alternative or the assist that covers it.

quiz.question: Your security team wants to block paste in the password field to stop attacks. What do you decide?
options: Allow paste and password manager autofill
Block paste, but add a “Show password” toggle
Block paste, and add a security question as a backup
quiz.why: A password with no help is a memory test. Paste and password managers are the mechanism that assists, so blocking them fails the rule, and a security question is just another memory test.

spec: State that every credential and code field allows paste and autofill.
Give password and code fields the right autocomplete tokens.
List the other login methods offered, such as passkey or email link, and where they appear.
review: What does this login ask me to remember, copy or solve?
Have you tried it with a password manager and paste?
If a CAPTCHA is here, what is the alternative?
tradeoff: Security teams sometimes block paste or add puzzles to stop bots. Blocking paste mostly stops password managers, which makes passwords weaker. Use passkeys, rate limits and invisible bot checks instead.
system: Make the code-entry component accept a pasted code across all its boxes, and never offer a paste-blocking option on password fields.
pitch: Every locked-out user is a support call. Letting password managers work is safer and cheaper.
